c.title: Proposal 2026-1
c.pre: A proposal to convene a constitutional convention for the purpose of drafting a general revision of the state constitution
c.q: Shall a convention of elected delegates be convened in 2027 to draft a general revision of the State Constitution for presentation to the state’s voters for their approval or rejection?

c.title: Proposal 2026-2
c.pre: A proposed initiated law to prohibit campaign contributions from certain regulated utilities and government contractors and apply campaign finance laws and regulations to additional types of political communications
c.q:
The proposal would:

• Prohibit regulated electric and gas utilities, contractors with over $250,000 annually in government contracts, and people and organizations with substantial connections to these utilities/contractors from making direct or indirect campaign contributions to those who run for or hold offices that impact them.

• Expand laws regulating spending on political communications, including those requiring disclosing donor information, to apply to communications clearly identifying candidates or ballot questions, even if they do not expressly advocate voting for/against them.

• Expressly apply the law requiring disclosure of who paid for political communications to internet political communications.

Should this proposal be adopted?

c.title: TUSCOLA COUNTY COUNTY VETERANS SERVICES MILLAGE RENEWAL
c.q: Shall the previously approved millage authorization in support of Tuscola County Veterans Services, reduced by the required millage rollbacks and which will expire in December, 2026, be renewed and the County of Tuscola, Michigan, be authorized to levy a millage of 0.1697 mill ($0.1697 per $1,000 of State Taxable Value) annually, for a period of six (6) years, 2027-2032 inclusive, on all taxable property within in Tuscola County to provide dedicated services and programs to veterans of the United States military and their qualified dependents within the county (“Veterans Services”)? The estimated revenue the County will collect in the first year of levy (2027) if the millage is approved is approximately $406,500. (This is a reauthorization and six-year extension of a millage levied in 2026, that will expire with the 2026 tax levy, rather than an increase.) To the extent required by law, a portion of the revenues collected from this millage (estimated to be approximately 0.6% in the first year), will be captured by or disbursed to the Caro Downtown Development Authority (“DDA”), Cass City DDA, Millington DDA and Vassar DDA.

c.title: TUSCOLA COUNTY COUNTY VETERANS SERVICES MILLAGE INCREASE
c.q: Shall the tax limitation on all taxable property within Tuscola County, Michigan, be increased and the County be authorized to levy a new millage in the amount of 0.03 mills ($0.03 per $1,000 of taxable value) annually, for six (6) years, 2027 to 2032 inclusive, to provide dedicated services and programs to veterans of the United States military and their qualified dependents within the County (“Veterans Services”)? The estimated revenue the County will collect in the first year of levy (2027) if the millage is approved is approximately $72,575. To the extent required by law, a portion of the revenues collected from this millage (estimated to be approximately 0.6% in the first year), will be captured by or disbursed to the Caro Downtown Development Authority (“DDA”), Cass City DDA, Millington DDA and Vassar DDA.

c.title: TUSCOLA TOWNSHIP PROPOSAL TO APPROVE EXTRA-VOTED ROAD IMPROVEMENT MILLAGE
c.q: Shall Tuscola Township impose an increase of up to 1 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution and levy it for four (4) years, 2026 through 2029, inclusive, for the purpose of local road repairs, upgrades, construction, improvement, dust control, and maintenance purposes, which 1 mill increase will raise an estimated $109,600 in the first year the millage is levied?

c.title: DAYTON TOWNSHIP ROAD MILLAGE
c.q: Shall the Township of Dayton be authorized to levy a millage of one (1) mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value of real property) for a period of three (3) years, 2027 to 2029 inclusive, for the purpose of maintaining and improving roads in the Township? If the millage is levied, the estimated revenue that will be collected in the first year from the levy in 2027 will be $74,000.

c.title: Saginaw Intermediate School District
c.pre: Area Career and Technical Education Millage Proposal
c.q:
This proposal will allow the intermediate school district to continue to levy millage previously approved by the electors for area career and technical education programs and restores millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963.

Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation of .9962 mill ($0.9962 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Saginaw Intermediate School District, Michigan, to provide funds for area career and technical education programs, be renewed for a period of 10 years, 2028 to 2037, inclusive; and also be increased by .0038 mill ($0.0038 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 10 years, 2028 to 2037, inclusive, the estimate of the revenue the intermediate school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2028 is approximately $7,082,354 from local property taxes authorized herein (this is a renewal of millage that will expire with the 2027 tax levy and a restoration of millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963)?

c.title: ALMER CHARTER TOWNSHIP ROAD MILLAGE PROPOSAL
c.q: Shall the tax limitation on all taxable property within Almer Charter Township, Tuscola County, Michigan, be increased and the Township be authorized to levy annually a new additional millage in an amount not to exceed 1.0 mill ($1.00 per each $1,000 of taxable value), for a period of four (4) years, 2026 through 2029 inclusive, for the purpose of improving, repairing, and maintaining roads in the Township? The estimate of the revenue the Township will collect in the first year of levy (2026) if the millage is approved is approximately $84,000.

c.title: VILLAGE OF CASS CITY POLICE DEPARTMENT
c.q: Shall the Village of Cass City impose an increase of 0.9932 mill ($0.9932 per $1,000 of taxable value) in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution and levy it for four (4) years, 2027 through 2030 inclusive, and shall be exclusively used for police activities, including road patrol, School Resource Officer, community policing, and emergency response within the Village of Cass City which 0.9932 mill increase will raise an estimated $74,397.00 in the first year the millage is levied. As required by Michigan law, a small portion of the millage shall be captured by the Cass City Downtown Development Authority.

c.title: COLUMBIA TOWNSHIP EMERGENCY SERVICES MILLAGE PROPOSAL
c.q: Shall the previously voted increase in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution on general ad valorem taxes within Columbia Township be renewed at 1.0 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) for the period of 2026 through 2033 inclusive for Emergency Fire and Ambulance Services and/or Equipment for the Township of Columbia; and shall the township levy such renewal in millage for said purpose, thereby raising in the first year an estimated $144,000.00.

c.title: COLUMBIA TOWNSHIP ROAD CONSTRUCTION MILLAGE RENEWAL
c.q: Shall the previously voted increase in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution on general ad valorem taxes within Columbia Township of 1.5 mills ($1.50 per $1000 of taxable value), reduced to 1.4927 mills ($1.4927 per $1000 of taxable value) by the required rollbacks and subject to further rollbacks for 2026, be renewed at up to 1.4927 mills ($1.4927 per $1000 of taxable value) for seven years, 2026 through 2033 inclusive, for new road construction; and shall the township levy such renewal in millage for said purpose, thereby raising in the first year an estimated $216,000.00?

c.title: AKRON TOWNSHIP EMERGENCY SERVICES MILLAGE PROPOSAL (RENEWAL)
c.q: Shall the limitation of the amount of property taxes which may be assessed each year against property in the Township of Akron, County of Tuscola, State of Michigan, be renewed for a period of five (5) years 2027 through 2031 inclusive up to the original levy of one (1) mill ($1.00 per $1,000.00 of taxable value, currently reduced to $0.9994 per each thousand dollars of taxable value to account for the Headlee reduction). Said millage to be used exclusively for fire and ambulance services and equipment as provided for by Section 6, Article IX of the 1963 Constitution of the State of Michigan. In the first year of the levy, this proposal will raise an estimated sum of $150,660.70
